title: Apoptotic Effect of Crude Scorpion Venom on Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma Cell Line versus Normal Human Epithelial Cell Line (In-vitro Study)
author: Doha Mohammed Afifi

Furthermore, the selective action of scorpion venom against cancer cells only, sparing normal cells, has also been reported (Díaz-García et al., 2013). However, a review article showed that the most of studies have focused on only inhibitory effects on cancer cells lines. Moradi et al., (2018) reported that the studies will be more valuable, if the inhibitory effects be assessed simultaneously in can cer cell line and normal cells. Arpornsuwan et al., (2014) and Tong -ngam et al., (2 015) studied BmKn -2 scorpion venom peptide and its antimicrobial and anticancer activities against human oral squamous cells carcinoma cell line (HSC-4). The BmKn-2 peptide killed HSC -4 cells through induction of apoptosis. Their results showed that scorpi on venom and its derived peptides are promising chemotherapeutic agents for oral cancer treatment; which needed to be confirmed by further investigations. . 6c. Onjective: The objective of this study is to investigate the apoptotic effect of crude scorpion venom on HNSCC cell line as well as normal human epithelial cell line, therefore providing a more selective, effective and less toxic possible treatment for such a malignancy.

steps.title: Prepare cell lines and media
steps.instruction: Obtain the head‑and‑neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) cell line and a normal human epithelial cell line from VACSERA (Cairo, Egypt) or ICTAR‑Egypt, culture each in its compatible nutrient medium, and keep them at 37 °C in a humidified 5 % CO₂ incubator.

steps.title: Seed cells for SRB assay
steps.instruction: Sub‑culture the cells into a 96‑well plate, adding enough volume to form a confluent monolayer (exact volume not specified).

steps.title: Perform SRB fixation and staining
steps.instruction: Incubate the monolayer for 48 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂; fix with 5 µL per well of 50 % trichloro‑acetic acid for 1 h using a multichannel pipette; wash wells with tap water and air‑dry for 1 h; add 50 µL Sulphorhodamine B stain to each well and incubate 30 min; wash with 5 % glacial acetic acid; recover bound stain with 100 µL EDTA buffer; treat half of the wells with crude scorpion venom (Leiurus quinquestriatus powder from Egy venom company, Cairo, Egypt) diluted in complete growth medium.

steps.title: Seed cells for MTT assay
steps.instruction: Plate 1 mL of cell suspension containing 5 × 10⁴–1 × 10⁵ cells per mL into each well of a 96‑well plate and incubate 24 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Treat cells with scorpion venom (MTT)
steps.instruction: After a 24‑72 h pre‑treatment with antibiotics/antifungal agents, remove the culture medium, wash cells with PBS, add crude scorpion venom (same source as above) in complete growth medium, incubate 48 h, then wash twice with PBS.

steps.title: Conduct MTT viability assay
steps.instruction: Add medium containing 0.5 mg/mL MTT to each well and incubate 4 h at 37 °C in a CO₂ incubator; aspirate the medium, solubilize the formazan crystals with dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO); measure absorbance at 570 nm using a BioTek FLX‑800 microplate reader; calculate % cytotoxicity = 1 – (mean absorbance of treated cells / mean absorbance of negative control) and % viability = 100 – % cytotoxicity.

steps.title: Lyse cells for Puma ELISA
steps.instruction: Collect cells from each condition, spin down 15 min at 1 200 rpm, discard supernatant, wash pellet once with cold PBS, resuspend in lysis buffer to 1.5 × 10⁶ cells/mL, incubate 1 h at room temperature with gentle shaking; centrifuge at 200 × g for 15 min, collect supernatant and dilute at least 1:50 in 1X assay buffer (5 µL supernatant + 245 µL buffer).

steps.title: Perform Puma ELISA assay
steps.instruction: Add prepared biotin‑conjugated antibody to each diluted sample well, wash, add streptavidin‑HRP solution, wash, add tetramethylbenzidine (TMB) substrate and incubate at room temperature, add stop solution, read absorbance immediately at 450 nm with an ELISA plate reader.

steps.title: Treat cells for flow‑cytometry
steps.instruction: Add crude scorpion venom to flasks at the predetermined IC₅₀ concentration, incubate 48 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Prepare cells for flow cytometry
steps.instruction: Harvest cells by trypsinization, obtain a single‑cell suspension, centrifuge 15 min at 1 500 rpm, aliquot 1 mL of cells into a 15 mL polypropylene tube, add 3 mL cold absolute ethanol, fix and wash twice with PBS, add Annexin V/propidium iodide staining solution and mix, add RNase stock solution and incubate, filter the suspension to remove aggregates.

steps.title: Analyze cell cycle by flow cytometry
steps.instruction: Run the stained cells on a flow cytometer (FACS) at 100–200 events per second, acquire data, and display results as frequency histograms and dot plots.

description: 2 II. Introduction: 6a. Statement of the problem: Squamous cell carcinoma arises from multiple anatomic subsites in the head and neck region . Current treatments involves a combination of surgery, radiotherapy and chemotherapy. Commonly used chemotherapeutic agents frequently affect normal human cells and cause severe side effects (Gerber, 2008 and Weeks et al., 2012). Moreover, cancer cells can develop resistance to these agents by cellular changes through multi-mechanism (Gatti & Zunino, 2005). Therefore, the devel opment of new therapeutic agents that can be used for effective, specific and safe treatment has gained interest (Tong-ngam et al., 2015). Scorpions and their venoms have been used in traditional medicine for thousands of years in China, India and Africa. The scorpion venom is a highly complex mixture of salts, nucleotides, biogenic amines, enzymes, mucoproteins, as well as peptides and proteins (e.g. neurotoxins). Yet, besides their neurotoxic activities, some have antitumor properties. In an incre asing number of pre -clinical and experimental researches, cell cycle arrest and apoptosis induction, as well as inhibition of cancer proliferation and metastasis have been demonstrated to be caused by some purified peptides and proteins with the help of crude scorpion venom under in-vitro or in-vivo conditions (Ding et al., 2014). PICO P1: Cultured human HNSCC cell line. P2: Cultured human epithelial cell line. I: Application of crude scorpion venom on both cell lines. C1: Cultured HNSCC cell line without venom application. C2: Cultured normal epithelial cell line without venom application. O: Assessment of cell viability, apoptosis and cell cycle phases in the 4 groups.
